# Model card: Rubric drafting

| | |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Suggest a screening rubric (criteria, evidence, score anchors) for a job. |
| Workflow | hire |
| Code | `pairly_hire.drafting.draft_rubric` |
| Prompt | `hire_rubric_draft` version `v1`, file SHA-256 `c094ca7edb30c1a3...` |
| Output schema | `Rubric` |
| Model tiers, cheapest first | `small` (anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, openai `gpt-6-luna`) then `large` (anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5`, openai `gpt-6.1-sol`) |
| Temperature | 0.0 |
| Output token limit | 4096 |
| Confidence threshold to accept | none |

## Inputs

The job title and description.

## Outputs

A `Rubric`, validated against the rubric schema.

## Human oversight

A person edits the draft and locks a version. Locking is a `lock` action that needs a second factor; only a locked rubric can score applications, and every score records the rubric version it used.

## Limits

* Criteria may be too broad or overlap; calibration shows where people and the AI disagree.
* The draft is not checked for job relatedness beyond what the person reviews.
* Every call is logged in `model_calls` (prompt version and hash, model, inputs, output, tokens, cost) and fails closed: no model means a person does the step.

They are not quality judgments: how good a draft is needs a live model and people.
